conjecture: FP_x^2 = FV · FP_y, so FP_x is the mean proportional between FV and FP_y (equivalently FV : FP_x = FP_x : FP_y).
reason: GF is a diameter. The tangent f is perpendicular to GF, so j (through F, parallel to f) is the tangent to c at F. V is where the tangents at F and E meet, so VF = VE. Angle GEF is 90° because it stands on the diameter GF, so triangle FED is right-angled at E. A point on its hypotenuse FD that is equidistant from F and E must be the circumcenter, so V is the midpoint of FD. Now place F at the origin with j as the x-axis. Then h1 is x = v, e is x = 2v, and P_x = (v, t). The ray FP_x meets e at K = (2v, 2t). The line y = 2t meets the perpendicular to FP_x at P_x in the point P_y = (v - t^2/v, 2t). As t varies, P_y traces the parabola y^2 = -4v(x - v). This parabola has focus F, vertex V, axis j and vertex tangent h1. The line m is the tangent to the parabola at P_y, and P_x is the foot of the perpendicular from the focus F to that tangent. This is Newton's Lemma XIV: the perpendicular from the focus to a tangent is the mean proportional between the focus-to-vertex and focus-to-contact distances. Algebraically, FP_x^2 = v^2 + t^2 and FV · FP_y = |v| · (v^2 + t^2)/|v| = v^2 + t^2. Numerical check: FP_x^2 ≈ 26.20 and FV · FP_y ≈ 2.3094 × 11.345 ≈ 26.20.
